name: Macro
first: Code that swiftc runs while it builds a program, which adds Swift code to the program where the macro is used.

dependsOn.why: The macro in the example is used inside a function, and expands to the function's name.
dependsOn.whyInExample: `#function` is written inside the function `pack(_:)`, and expands to its name.

sil.shows: swiftc replaced #function with the text pack(_:) when it built the program.

what.is: A macro is code that swiftc runs while it builds the program, and that adds Swift code where the macro is used. A freestanding macro is written with a number sign, as `#function`, and is replaced by the code it expands to. An attached macro is written with an at sign before a declaration, and adds code to that declaration.
what.afterExample: `#function` is a macro from the Swift standard library. swiftc replaced it with the name of the function it is in, so each call prints {{pack(_:)}} first.
what.problem: Some code follows the same pattern every time, such as code that writes a function's name, or code that tells SwiftUI when a property changes. Written by hand, it is repeated, and can fall out of date. A macro writes it when the program is built, from the code around it.
what.how: When swiftc builds the program, it expands each macro: it runs the macro's own code, and puts the code that the macro writes into the program. Swift's documentation says that a macro only adds code, and never deletes or changes the code you wrote. swiftc then checks the added code, as it checks yours.

when.text: Use the macros that Swift and SwiftUI provide where they save writing the same code by hand. `@Observable` is an attached macro: it adds code to the class it is written before, so that SwiftUI can tell when its properties change:
Don't expect to find the added code in your file: swiftc adds it while it builds the program. In Xcode, Expand Macro in the Editor menu shows the code that a macro adds.

parts.name: The macro `#function`, line 2
parts.text: A number sign before a name uses a freestanding macro. `#function` is a freestanding macro from the Swift standard library. swiftc expands it to a string that holds the name of the function it is in, `pack(_:)`.

steps.text: swiftc expanded `#function` on line 2 to the name of the function it is in, so line 2 prints {{pack(_:) packs Socks}}.
Line 6 calls `pack(_:)` again, and line 2 prints {{pack(_:) packs Map}}.

end.text: `#function` was replaced by the name of the function it is in when swiftc built the program, not while the program ran.
